findings.evidence: Lines 198-201: `have h := hg.polarization (deltaTarget K) K.q; rw [add_comm] at h; rw [MX2, pX, tMom, DisKinematics.Q2]; linarith`. Mathlib's lemma is `IsSymm.polarization (x y) (hB) : B x y = (B (x + y) (x + y) - B x x - B y y) / 2` (mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Properties.lean:138).
findings.fix: Either give explicit arguments (`rw [add_comm (deltaTarget K) K.q] at h`), or drop `polarization` and expand directly with the idiom used at `Exclusive/Kinematics/Basic.lean:133,142`: after `rw [MX2, pX, tMom, DisKinematics.Q2]`, `simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]` then `linarith [hg.eq K.q (deltaTarget K)]`.
findings.issue: `rw [add_comm] at h` has no arguments: it flips whichever `?a + ?b` matches first in the polarization hypothesis, solely so `g (Δ + q) (Δ + q)` becomes the `g (q + Δ) (q + Δ)` atom `linarith` needs. Which addition is rewritten is invisible to the reader and depends on the exact shape of `IsSymm.polarization`.

findings.evidence: Lines 214-218. The rest of the layer expands bilinear arguments with `simp only [map_add, map_sub, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.sub_apply]` plus `linarith`/`linear_combination` (Exclusive/Kinematics/Basic.lean:133, 139, 142-143), which is insensitive to term order.
findings.fix: Expand the goal instead of steering the hypothesis: `rw [MY2, tMom, deltaTarget]; simp only [map_sub, LinearMap.sub_apply]; linarith [hg.eq K.pPrime K.p]` (or state a shared `g (a - b) (a - b) = g a a - 2 * g a b + g b b` helper under `hg` and reuse it here and in `MX2_eq_...`).
findings.issue: Same pattern in `MY2_eq_p_sq_sub_two_mul_apply_p_deltaTarget_add_tMom`: `rw [← sub_eq_add_neg, deltaTarget, sub_sub_cancel] at h` is a four-step, order-sensitive rewrite chain on a hypothesis (it depends on `P + -Δ` appearing before any other `a + -b`, and on `P - (P - P')` matching `sub_sub_cancel` after unfolding), which hides why the hypothesis ends up in the form `linarith` consumes.

summary: Proofs are short, structural, and free of show/change or defeq tricks; hypotheses are all load-bearing. The two square-expansion proofs steer `polarization` with position-sensitive rewrites (an untargeted `add_comm`, and a `← sub_eq_add_neg, deltaTarget, sub_sub_cancel` chain inside a hypothesis) instead of the robust expansion idiom already used elsewhere in this layer.
